newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-ROCCA HANGS ON TO LEAD IN RAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ROCCA HANGS ON TO LEAD IN RAIN.

text.p: After a three-and-half-hour suspension for torrential rain, players stayed out on the Scandinavian Masters course until dusk on Thursday and Italy's Costantino Rocca boosted his Ryder Cup hopes by taking an early first round lead.
Rocca, ninth in Europe's Ryder Cup table, shrugged off injury problems to card a seven-under-par 65 and lead by a stroke from another Cup hopeful, Ireland's Padraig Harrington.
Spain's Ignacio Garrido, Joakim Haeggman of Sweden and England's Mark Roe were a further stroke back.

Another Spaniard, Jose Maria Olazabal, currently holding the 10th and last place in Europe's Ryder Cup table, was still a threat to the leaderboard, however, as he moved three-under-par with five holes still to play.

Rocca established his lead with seven birdies and no bogeys, discarding the rib-support which he has needed since suffering the injury two months ago which caused him to pull out of the U.S. Open and slip down the Ryder Cup table.
"I took off the bandage today and felt really free, the first time I've been able to turn and swing properly for a long time," said Rocca. "It was my best round of the year and I feel good.
"I know I have to do well out of the five events left before the team is selected and this is a good start."
